II.2. Transmission Matrix Approach

The transmission matrix approach outlined below is used to determine the complex transmission coefficient of a multi-section cavity which has been deduced by S. O’Brien and E. P. O’Reilly.² The method is restated here as insight into the novel engineering approach. For a multi-layer system, as in Figure 1, the complex transmission coefficient with one slot is found by considering a matrix product given by
(E₀ ; r̃E₀) = T₁₀ P₁ T₂₁ P₂ T₃₂ P₃ T₃₀ (t̃E₀ ; 0) ≡ (t̃E₀ ; 0), (II.1)
where T_ji = (t_ij)⁻¹ (1 r_ij ; r_ij 1) (II.2)
and P_i = (exp(−ik_iz L_i) 0 ; 0 exp(ik_iz L_i)) (II.3)
are the transmission and propagation matrices, respectively.⁹ The transmission and reflection coefficients at an interface and for normal incidence are given by
t_ij = 2n_i/(n_i+n_j), r_ij = (n_i−n_j)/(n_i+n_j).

The transmission coefficient, t̃, of the device is then given by S₁₁⁻¹ of the scattering matrix. In this work, the effective refractive index step, Δn, is treated as real and since typically Δn/n ≪ 1, where n is the effective index of the cavity, only first-order terms to order Δn/n are retained in the product of Equation II.2.
